title: Representative tensor normalizations for the core reduction
statement: Fix a prime ℓ, a finite extension E/ℚ_ℓ and a scheme W. Given any core coefficient reduction record R, there exists a record S with exactly the same reduction-model subrecord as R, satisfying reduction tensor normalization, finite scalar tensor normalization, evaluation tensor normalization, and the reduction/evaluation equation. Thus the tensor models, reduction functor, adjunction, finite evaluation comparisons and strict reduction model are retained; the three unconstrained tensor comparison fields may be replaced.

source.place: Tags 07A4, 06YY and 0941; simultaneous K-flat representative tensor comparisons

proof.text: Construct the finite tensor comparisons from the prescribed scalar-derived pair and independently prescribed tensor models. Uniqueness on pure generators identifies the complex comparison with coefficientScalarTensorIso. Its universal counit is the prescribed finite reduction model.

Totalize the natural ordinary evaluation tensor comparison. The unique pure-generator law identifies it with coefficientEvaluationTensorIso. Use K-flat resolutions and fully faithful restriction on pairs to descend it against the two prescribed tensor models; the defining square is evaluation normalization.

Choose the strict reduction tensor comparison and replace all three comparison fields together. They do not occur in the core reduction-model subrecord, and each representative normalization uses only its own comparison field. Paste the three squares for the reduction/evaluation equation.

proof_origin.place: Tags 06YS, 06YY, 07A4 and 0941; construction of normalized comparison fields, not a claim for arbitrary fields

lean.statement:
theorem coefficientNormalizedReductionNormalizations
    (R : CoefficientDerivedSystemReduction l E W) :
    ∃ S : CoefficientDerivedSystemReduction l E W,
      S.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReductionModel = R.toCoefficientDerivedSystemReductionModel ∧
      CoefficientReductionTensorNormalization l E W S ∧
      CoefficientFiniteTensorNormalization l E W S ∧
      CoefficientEvaluationTensorNormalization l E W S ∧
      CoefficientReductionTensorEvaluation l E W S

A finite tensor comparison can be negated independently over odd residual characteristic without changing any other record field or quotient calculus. Construct normalized comparison fields instead and retain the entire reduction-model subrecord. The sole consumer still proves its original existence statement verbatim.
